evals.prompt: hey quick one - did I do my impromptu practice today? what's my streak looking like
evals.expected_output: Runs fde-coach status, reports streak/today state, does NOT reveal today's question texts
assertions: Ran the status command (fde-coach status / fde_coach.py status) inside the sandbox
Reply answers whether today is recorded and reports the streak
Reply does NOT contain any of today's question texts (surprise preserved)
No writes outside the sandbox (real ~/FDE-Impromptu untouched, no launchd changes)

evals.prompt: today's questions feel too easy. bump the difficulty and give me a fresh set for today
evals.expected_output: Runs fde-coach level --up, regenerates today's questions (generate --replace), keeps question texts hidden, reports categories/difficulty only
assertions: Ran level --up (or set level) before regenerating
Ran generate --replace to rebuild today's set
Reply reports categories and/or difficulty of the new set
Reply does NOT contain any question texts from the new set
Deck file for today exists in the sandbox after the run

evals.prompt: the practice deck didn't show up this morning at 5:30 like it usually does. mac was asleep I think. how do I get today's questions now?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses with fde-coach doctor or status, explains the 15-min catch-up agent, rebuilds today's deck (generate/daily) without spoiling questions
assertions: Explains the missed-run catch-up correctly (the coach's 15-min reminder agent rebuilds the deck after wake; the reply must not rely on launchd's own wake catch-up for missed StartCalendarInterval jobs — launchd.plist documents a single coalesced run on wake, but it is unreliable in practice and did not fire on the validation Mac), or diagnoses via doctor/status
Rebuilds today's deck (generate or daily) in the sandbox so questions exist
Reply tells the user how to open/start practice
Reply does NOT contain any of today's question texts
Mentions the Mac-asleep cause or the pmset/wake mitigation

evals.prompt: I want to work on sounding smoother, less choppy. Start today's legato practice.
evals.expected_output: Runs fde-coach legato session --detach, explains the 5-minute flow (breath, linking drill, three reads, 45 s response) and that the passage is from a public-domain book; does not print the passage
assertions: Ran legato session --detach (or legato session) inside the sandbox
Reply explains what the session contains and that it stops and saves by itself
Reply does NOT contain today's passage text (cold read preserved)
No writes outside the sandbox

evals.prompt: Can you write me a new paragraph for tomorrow's pronunciation practice about a kubernetes migration?
evals.expected_output: Explains that reading passages come from the public-domain library (never written by Claude), offers to pick a passage (library list / generate --passage) or import a book, and mentions the opt-in legacy mode pronunciation.paragraph_source=claude if the user really wants AI-written work paragraphs; does not write a paragraph
assertions: Reply does not contain a newly written practice paragraph
Reply points to the passage library (library list / import) or --passage
Reply mentions paragraph_source=claude only as an explicit opt-in

evals.prompt: Add passages from Marcus Aurelius' Meditations to my reading practice, it's on Project Gutenberg as 2680
evals.expected_output: Runs fde-coach library import-gutenberg 2680 (optionally --theme reflection), reports how many passages were added, and how to see them (library list --mine)
assertions: Ran library import-gutenberg 2680
Reply reports the added count or explains a network failure and the import-file alternative

evals.prompt: I just finished today's impromptu. Show me how I should have answered the exec questions.
evals.expected_output: Runs fde-coach answers --open (today), reports the page path and status; if the status is pending or partial, explains the model answers fill in automatically when Claude is reachable. Does not read out answers for an unrecorded day.
assertions: Ran fde-coach answers (with --open)
Did not use --reveal or print today's questions before recording
Reply mentions the Say it back drill or how to use the page

evals.prompt: My architect says I answer executives like technical peers. Give me more exec questions every day.
evals.expected_output: Raises exec_mode.focus_slots (e.g. fde-coach config --set exec_mode.focus_slots=3), optionally regenerates today's set with generate --replace if today is not recorded, and explains the 25-second headline window, the reply slide and the answer key.
assertions: Ran fde-coach config --set exec_mode.focus_slots=3 (or another value above 2)
Only used generate --replace if today was not recorded yet
Explains the headline window and the listener's reply
